REFERENS – the game’s subdivision according to SvFF’s game model: Attacks, the stages: Game Building · Contring · Coming to Shots and Making Goals. Defense Games, the stages: Recovery of the ball · Prevent game buildup · Prevent and save shots. Restorations: Conversion to assault (when we win the ball) and Reset to Defense (when we lose the ball). Game surfaces in depth: Exit surface, Play surface 1, Play surface 2, Play surface 3. In width: outer, inner and central corridor. Rolls in attacks: 1st striker = the player on the ball (playing in favor: open or closed surface, pressed or unpressed, fit or operate). 2nd attacker = the nearest co-player (playability, scanning, positioning - "diamond"). 3rd striker = further away (game depth, game width, movement, contender protection). Roles in Defence: 1st defender = closest to the player on the ball (1 v 1, press or cover). 2nd and 3rd defenders (compact team, mark or cover, close the inside, collective movements; 3rd defenders also have contradiction protection. Legal principles: In seizures – play where the best advantage is. In defense – quickly compact, close the inside, prevent games through and behind the team, press the player on the ball against the outer corridor. Advantage may be numeric (we are more), positional (better placed), relationshipal (better collaborative) or qualitative (better in the situation). METODIK as in UEFA C, B and A trainings: - Gaming exercises with direction, resistance and decisions. Lots of ball contact and no lines. Arrange the surface, rules and points so that the chosen stage often occurs and is rewarded. - Coaching both with instruction and with questions that cause players to discover the solution themselves. Customize by age: 6-9 years of play and game with small teams with few rules; 10-12 years of simple game exercises focusing on 1st attackers and 1st defenders; 13-15 years of groups and 2/3rd strikers and defenders; 16 years and older team principles, game surfaces and corridors. Level UEFA C: simple organization and a clear principle. UEFA B: group collaboration, roles and stages. UEFA A: team level, game surfaces, corridors, type of advantage and clear load (work and rest).

SPELSTIL – German school (DFB): joy, intensity and repetition in each exercise. Small game forms on multiple plans simultaneously, high net playing time and no standing queues. Quick conversion game: after ball loss, the team immediately sets after the ball (Gegenpressing), after the ball win, the team plays quickly and vertically towards goals. Short, intense periods of about 3 minutes of rest. For children: 3 versus 3 v 2 small goals per team, rotation at each goal or no later than 2 minutes, kicks are replaced by running or fitting in, and the coach allows the children to solve the task themselves during the game.

SPELSTIL – Italian School (FIGC/Coverciano): Training by Principles The defence is short and narrow with zone defence, coverage and inerted signals for when the team steps out in the press, and the team reacts directly to ball loss. In seizures, positioning games with jokers are used to train the commuter movement between the midfielders, width, penetration and passage in between or behind the lines. Work in chains on the edges and in the legislative parts (defense against seizures). For children: the game as a teacher, from exercise to game, duels and collaboration, variants and self-judgment.

SPELSTIL – Spanish school (Juego de posición): ball holding is the first goal. The fitting should be hard and go to the foot that makes the reception easy, and the first touch is directed. Positioning is a weapon of attack: the surfaces are filled sensibly with width and depth, and everyone knows what the other positions should do. The relationships between nearby players are central. Players learn through the game rather than through isolated moments – the concept is played. Typical formats: round dose with the players in their positions, possession games without goals, positioning games and real-life situational games (e.g., 8 versus 6).
SPELSTIL: mix elements from Spanish, German and Italian schools when it suits the exercise.
